h1: The 6 Best Wireless Printers for Home Offices of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Wireless Home Office Printers: Ranked
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six wireless printers for home offices, covering inkjet, supertank and laser, with duplex and ADF options, sorted by need.
summary: A home-office printer should connect without drama and feed multi-page jobs. The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e is our top pick for its ADF, duplex and multi-device support. The Epson EcoTank ET-2800 wins on ink economy, the Brother laser is best for text, and the Canon TS6520 helps with connection troubleshooting.
intro: The usual mistake is judging a printer by its purchase price. Over a year of home-office printing, ink or toner costs and the hassle of reconnecting to WiFi matter more than the upfront bucket.

We reviewed eight listings, removed a near-duplicate HP OfficeJet Pro and a basic Canon, and ranked six on connectivity, duplex and document feeding, consumables and price bucket. Findings rest on listing specs.

products.name: HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: ADF, duplex and multi-device WiFi in one home-office inkjet.
products.description:
The OfficeJet Pro 8125e supports multiple devices over WiFi, has an automatic document feeder and duplex printing, and includes a 3-month Instant Ink trial. The listing falls in the $50-100 bucket.

It leads because feeding stacks and printing both sides are what an office actually does daily. The Canon TS6520 offers duplex but no ADF in its listing.

Buy it for a household of several users. The caveat is that Instant Ink is a subscription after the trial.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-2800 Wireless Color All-in-One Supertank Printer
products.verdict: Cartridge-free ink tanks that mean fewer refill interruptions.
products.description:
The EcoTank ET-2800 is a cartridge-free supertank all-in-one with scan and copy, a compact body and setup that does not depend on a WPS button. It is in the $100-200 bucket.

It ranks second because the listing mentions no ADF or duplex, but its long-lasting ink supply suits heavy printing. HP wins on features, Epson on running cost.

Choose it if you print steadily and hate cartridge runs. The caveat is the higher upfront bucket.
products.idealFor: Steady printing with low ink hassle.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A compact black-and-white laser with duplex, copy and scan.
products.description:
The Brother DCP-L2640DW is a compact monochrome laser with WiFi, duplex, copy and scan, a Refresh Subscription toner trial and Alexa support. It is priced somewhere from $200 to $500.

It ranks third because black-only printing excludes color work, yet lasers stay ready after long idle periods. It costs more upfront than any inkjet here.

Pick it for contracts and documents. The caveat is no color.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A small OLED shows WiFi status when connections drop.
products.description:
The TS6520 uses app-guided WiFi setup and a 1.42 inch OLED display that shows connection status, plus duplex printing and a compact body. It is in the $50-100 bucket.

It ranks fourth because it lacks an ADF but its status screen helps diagnose dropped connections. It undercuts the HP in features.

Buy it if WiFi trouble worries you. The caveat is the small feature list.
products.idealFor: Anyone who has fought printer WiFi before.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: App-guided setup for routers without a WPS button.
products.description:
The DeskJet 4355 joins WiFi through the HP Smart app so no WPS button is needed, adds a 3-month Instant Ink trial and AI-capable printing features in a compact body. The listing falls in the $50-100 bucket.

It ranks fifth because it skips the ADF and duplex shown on the OfficeJet. Setup simplicity is its pitch.

It fits light home use. The caveat is the basic office feature set.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: WiFi with an automatic document feeder and legacy fax on a budget.
products.description:
The TR4720 offers WiFi, an automatic document feeder, mobile printing and a built-in fax. Expect it in the $50 to $100 bucket.

It ranks last since fax is a legacy feature few home offices use, and duplex is not highlighted. The ADF at this price is its draw.

It suits multi-page scanning on a budget. The caveat is that fax is rarely needed.

whatMatters.detail: Some printers need a router WPS button, while app-guided setups do not. A stable connection saves hours. Look for app setup or no WPS dependency in the specs.
An automatic document feeder scans stacks and duplex prints both sides. Both matter for office work. Check the listing names each separately.
Cartridge costs add up. Supertank printers use bottles, lasers use toner, and some inkjets lean on subscription plans. Read the ink system line before buying.
Laser monochrome is cheap for text, while color inkjets handle charts and photos. Match to what you print.
Several people printing from phones and laptops need multi-device WiFi. Look for the phrase in the specs.

howToChoose.intro: Pages per month steer you to the right ink system.

cards.label: Inkjet
cards.text: Color at lower upfront cost. The HP and Canon models plus the Epson EcoTank are inkjet.

cards.label: Laser
cards.text: Sharp black text and low idle risk. The Brother DCP-L2640DW is the laser option.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should default to inkjet unless they print text almost exclusively.

howToChoose.subheading: For Remote Workers Scanning Contracts Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: An automatic document feeder, duplex and reliable WiFi.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e lists an ADF and duplex, and the Canon TR4720 lists an ADF at a budget.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print daily and want low ink fuss, pointing to the Epson EcoTank or Brother laser.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Printing is occasional, in which case the HP DeskJet 4355 suffices.

faq.q: Do I need WPS on my router?
faq.a: Not for the HP DeskJet or Epson EcoTank, which list setup that does not depend on a WPS button.

faq.q: Is a laser better than an inkjet for a home office?
faq.a: For text, yes. For color work an inkjet is more flexible.

faq.q: Is the EcoTank worth it over a cheap inkjet?
faq.a: If you print regularly, yes, since cartridge-free tanks lower interruptions. For occasional printing a cheaper model is fine.
Ignoring the ink cost. A low upfront price can hide an expensive consumable.

faq.q: How do I set up wireless printing?
faq.a: Use the maker's app to join your WiFi, then add the printer on your phone or computer.
HP's trial lasts three months. After that it is a subscription, so decide before the trial ends.

finalTake: The HP OfficeJet Pro 8125e is the best wireless printer for most home offices thanks to its ADF, duplex and multi-device support. Choose the Epson EcoTank for low ink fuss, the Brother for text and the Canon TS6520 if WiFi has burned you. Estimate your yearly pages first.
